drivingQuestion: Why does taking not constitute misuse while giving to another does?

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא הוּא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֲבֵירוֹ?! אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּגִזְבָּר, הַמְּסוּרוֹת לוֹ, עָסְקִינַן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that if one takes a stone or a beam belonging to the Temple treasury, he is not liable for misuse, but if he gives it to another he is liable for misuse. The Gemara asks: «What is different» with regard to «him» retaining possession of the item, «and what is different» with regard to him giving it to «another,» that he is rendered liable when he gives it to another? «Shmuel said: We are dealing with a treasurer [begizbar]» of the Temple, «to whom» the consecrated property «is given.» Since all the consecrated property is meant to be in his possession and charge, he is not guilty of misuse, provided that he does not transfer it to another.
